rawItems.question: Where did the four young rabbits live with their mother?
rawItems.answer: In a sand-bank underneath the root of a very big fir-tree.
evidenceQuotes:
They lived with their Mother in a sand-bank, underneath the root of a
very big fir-tree.

rawItems.question: Which siblings went down the lane to gather blackberries?
rawItems.answer: Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cottontail.
evidenceQuotes:
Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cottontail, who were good little bunnies, went
down the lane to gather blackberries:

rawItems.question: What errand did Mrs. Rabbit go on after telling the little rabbits where they could go?
rawItems.answer: She went through the wood to the baker’s, where she bought brown bread and five currant buns.
evidenceQuotes:
Then old Mrs. Rabbit took a basket and her umbrella, and went through
the wood to the baker's. She bought a loaf of brown bread and five
currant buns.

rawItems.question: Who called Peter a thief, and what was Peter doing when he did so?
rawItems.answer: Mr. McGregor called “Stop thief!” while chasing Peter after finding him near the cucumber frame.
evidenceQuotes:
But round the end of a cucumber frame, whom should he meet but Mr.
McGregor!

Mr. McGregor was on his hands and knees planting out young cabbages,
but he jumped up and ran after Peter, waving a rake and calling out,
'Stop thief!'

rawItems.question: Why did Peter lose his jacket?
rawItems.answer: Its large buttons caught in a gooseberry net while he was running away.
evidenceQuotes:
he had not unfortunately
run into a gooseberry net, and got caught by the large buttons on his
jacket.

Peter wriggled out just in time, leaving his jacket
behind him.

rawItems.question: How did the old mouse respond when Peter asked her the way to the gate?
rawItems.answer: She shook her head because she could not answer with a large pea in her mouth.
evidenceQuotes:
Peter asked her the way to
the gate, but she had such a large pea in her mouth that she could not
answer. She only shook her head at him.

rawItems.question: What sequence of events led Peter from being trapped in the gooseberry net to hiding in the tool-shed?
rawItems.answer: He wriggled free of the net and left his jacket behind, then rushed into the tool-shed and jumped into a can.
evidenceQuotes:
Peter wriggled out just in time, leaving his jacket
behind him.
And rushed into the tool-shed, and jumped into a can.

rawItems.question: What did Peter see at the pond, and why did he leave without speaking to the cat?
rawItems.answer: He saw a white cat staring at gold-fish and left because he had heard about cats from his cousin, little Benjamin Bunny.
evidenceQuotes:
A white cat was staring at some
gold-fish, she sat very, very still, but now and then the tip of her
tail twitched as if it were alive.

Peter thought it best to go away
without speaking to her; he had heard about cats from his cousin,
little Benjamin Bunny.

rawItems.question: How did Peter learn that the white cat might be dangerous?
rawItems.answer: He had heard about cats from his cousin, little Benjamin Bunny.
evidenceQuotes:
he had heard about cats from his cousin,
little Benjamin Bunny.

rawItems.question: How did the sparrows help Peter after he became caught in the net?
rawItems.answer: They flew to him and implored him to exert himself after hearing his sobs.
evidenceQuotes:
his sobs were
overheard by some friendly sparrows, who flew to him in great
excitement, and implored him to exert himself.

rawItems.question: What two things did Mr. McGregor do with the clothes Peter lost?
rawItems.answer: He hung up the jacket and shoes for a scare-crow to frighten the blackbirds.
evidenceQuotes:
Mr. McGregor hung up the little jacket and the shoes for a scare-crow
to frighten the blackbirds.

rawItems.question: What did Mrs. Rabbit give Peter that evening, and what instruction accompanied it?
rawItems.answer: She made him camomile tea and gave him a dose, with the instruction to take one table-spoonful at bed-time.
evidenceQuotes:
His mother put him to bed, and made some camomile tea; and she gave a
dose of it to Peter!
'One table-spoonful to be taken at bed-time.'

rawItems.question: What did Peter’s mother give him, and what did Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail have for supper?
rawItems.answer: Peter’s mother gave him a dose of camomile tea. Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail had bread and milk and blackberries for supper.
evidenceQuotes:
His mother put him to bed, and made some camomile tea; and she gave a
dose of it to Peter!

But Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail had bread and milk and
blackberries for supper.

rawItems.question: What did Peter see when he peeped over the wheelbarrow, and what did he do after getting down?
rawItems.answer: He saw Mr. McGregor hoeing onions, with his back turned towards Peter and the gate beyond him. Peter got down quietly and started running along a straight walk behind some black-currant bushes.
evidenceQuotes:
The first thing he saw was Mr. McGregor hoeing onions. His back was
turned towards Peter, and beyond him was the gate!

Peter got down very quietly off the wheelbarrow; and started running
as fast as he could go, along a straight walk behind some
black-currant bushes.

rawItems.question: How did Peter get from the wheelbarrow to safety outside the garden?
rawItems.answer: He quietly got down, ran along a straight walk behind black-currant bushes, and slipped underneath the gate.
evidenceQuotes:
Peter got down very quietly off the wheelbarrow; and started running
as fast as he could go, along a straight walk behind some
black-currant bushes.

He slipped underneath the gate, and was safe at last in the wood
outside the garden.

rawItems.question: Whose accident does Mrs. Rabbit mention, and what does she say happened afterward?
rawItems.answer: She says their Father had an accident there and was put in a pie by Mrs. McGregor.
evidenceQuotes:
'Now my dears,' said old Mrs. Rabbit one morning, 'you may go into
the fields or down the lane, but don't go into Mr. McGregor's garden:
your Father had an accident there; he was put in a pie by Mrs.
McGregor.'

rawItems.question: How did Peter’s escape from the garden compare with his arrival there?
rawItems.answer: He squeezed under the gate to enter and later slipped underneath it to leave.
evidenceQuotes:
Peter, who was very naughty, ran straight away to Mr. McGregor's
garden, and squeezed under the gate!

He slipped underneath the gate, and was safe at last in the wood
outside the garden.

rawItems.question: What events connect Peter’s sneeze to Mr. McGregor chasing him again?
rawItems.answer: Peter sneezed while Mr. McGregor was searching the tool-shed, and Mr. McGregor immediately went after him.
evidenceQuotes:
Presently Peter sneezed--'Kertyschoo!' Mr. McGregor was after him in
no time.

rawItems.question: What does Peter’s earlier shoe loss and the mention of another lost outfit suggest about his history of getting into trouble?
rawItems.answer: It suggests this was not his first lost outfit: his mother says it was the second jacket and pair of shoes he had lost in a fortnight.
evidenceQuotes:
He lost one of his shoes among the cabbages, and the other shoe
amongst the potatoes.

It was the
second little jacket and pair of shoes that Peter had lost in a
fortnight!

rawItems.question: How did the old mouse’s response to Peter’s request differ from the cat’s response to his presence?
rawItems.answer: The mouse shook her head when she could not answer Peter, while the cat sat very still as she watched the gold-fish; Peter chose to leave without speaking to the cat.
evidenceQuotes:
Peter asked her the way to
the gate, but she had such a large pea in her mouth that she could not
answer. She only shook her head at him.

A white cat was staring at some
gold-fish, she sat very, very still, but now and then the tip of her
tail twitched as if it were alive. Peter thought it best to go away
without speaking to her;
